data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The generator produces an unfair distribution over 10000 draws because the LCG's modulus (2^31) is not divisible by 6, causing modulo bias in the face-mapping (X_n mod 6) that persists at this horizon and pushes at least one face count outside two standard deviations of the uniform expectation.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The LCG orbit from seed 42 happens to visit residue classes mod 6 in a proportion that exactly cancels the modulo-6 imbalance of the 2^31 states, keeping all counts within tolerance.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The structural modulo bias exists but is small enough that over only 10000 steps the observed counts remain within two standard deviations for all six faces.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The LCG's low-order bits (which determine X mod 6) have better equidistribution than the state-space partition argument suggests, mitigating the bias.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The LCG state evolves in Z/(2^31)Z. The map die_n = 1 + (X_n mod 6) partitions the 2^31 states into six residue classes mod 6. Since 2^31 = 2147483648 = 6*357913941 + 2, the residues 0 and 1 each get 357913942 states while residues 2..5 get 357913941 states. This creates a deterministic structural bias favoring faces 1 and 2 over faces 3..6. Over 10000 steps, the LCG orbit from seed 42 samples this uneven partition, and the cumulative bias is large enough to exceed the two-sigma fairness window for at least one face.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
